verdicts.reason: AGENTS.md:14 still requires GO before --apply; line 76 only exempts the plan/review/build delegation chain from human approval pauses and does not mention --apply. It is an ambiguity that could be read as overriding the GO rule, not an explicit override.

Grep of queue_hud_src finds QueueHudPerformCastSpell only in exports.def:6 and kotor2-steam-aspyr.hooks.toml:31. There is no definition, so the linker fails on the export, matching the known build_check ld error.
The docstring (line 11) promises a static-invariants step and main() (123-235) has none. The claim is correct, but it is a documentation/coverage mismatch, not a wrong verdict in code that exists.

run_tests returns (True,'No specific tests requested.') for empty --test (98-99) and the PASS message at 194 says 'tests passing'. Behaviour is as described, but the flag is optional by design; the defect is the misleading message and a PASS with zero checks.
Scope is checked only when --scope is given (151-152) and PASS still prints 'scope clean' at 194. The wording is misleading, but --scope is opt-in, so it is not a silent bypass of a requested check.

narrow_plan_to_gog_scoping (337-359) does drop non-build tests, clear gaps and add a note with no Steam check. This is the documented intent (docstring) and is gated by an is_k2addr_gog_only_diff caller. The risk lies in the accuracy of that predicate, which I did not read here.

b_proc is created at 1007-1015 and only its stdout is parsed with PASS/FAIL regexes (1017-1051). returncode is never read, so a crash or non-zero exit without a 'FAIL build:' line adds no FAIL or ERROR.

NamedTemporaryFile(delete=False) at 1068 guarantees the file exists, so the is_file() check at 1089 is always true. An empty or invalid JSON makes the except at 1112 swallow the error, the else branch at 1114-1116 is dead, and proc.returncode is ignored. A crashed run_tests therefore yields no FAIL or ERROR. This is a real silent-pass path, but it needs a runner crash, so high rather than critical.

Line 1094 does default a missing status to PASS. This only matters if run_tests.py emits results without a status; I found no evidence it does. It is a fail-open default, so I judged it a hardening issue.

A suites.toml parse failure does 'except Exception: return' (444-447), silently dropping suite edges. This makes the plan under-select tests on a malformed file, but it takes a corrupt tracked TOML, and the failure is loud elsewhere (the suites are used by run_tests).

The substring logic at 509/518 does match everything when m_name is '' (name default ''), and the first dict-order hit wins. It requires a manifest with no name, and the id default is a non-empty path, so impact depends on whether such manifests exist.

include_build_tier and include_wine (856-860) are computed before positional filters are merged into target_ids (864-868), so positional 'wine:x' or 'suite:build-check' will not enable those tiers. The --id and --ids-file routes are processed earlier (830-833) and work, and compat_check uses --ids-file with --build/--wine. The bug is real only for positional use.

Line 871-872 filters items to target_ids with no check that anything is left. A grep for any no-tests or empty-selection guard in run_tests.py found none, so a stale or mistyped id gives '0 passed' and exit 0 unless the later code treats it differently (I did not read the return path at 982-995).

cross_file.evidence: compat_check passes test ids via --ids-file and ignores proc.returncode when the JSON file exists, but is empty (compat_check.py:1089-1113). run_tests.py filters items to target_ids with no empty-selection check (871-872) and exits 0 on zero tests. Both fail open: a stale or typo'd id, or a runner crash, gives a green compat result.
cross_file.why_it_matters: The compat gate can report success having run no tests, and it will still say so in the RESULT line and the exit code.
cross_file.suggested_investigation: Run compat_check with a bogus id in the plan and with run_tests.py forced to crash early. Compare exit codes. Check whether any caller (pre_install_gate) treats compat_check exit 0 as evidence.

cross_file.evidence: The export and the H10 hook binding both name QueueHudPerformCastSpell, and the symbol has no definition in queue_hud_src.
cross_file.why_it_matters: The DLL cannot link, so the H10 detour has no target. A fresh kpatch cannot be built until the definition lands or the hook and export are removed together.
cross_file.suggested_investigation: Check git history for where the QueueHudPerformCastSpell definition was lost or never added. Compare the hook's consumed bytes and exit address in the toml against the intended detour once it exists.

clusters.root_cause: Test and build runners ignore subprocess return codes and empty selections, so crashes and nothing-ran cases report PASS.
agent_diff_check reports PASS and 'scope clean/tests passing' even when no scope, test or static check was requested or run.
TOML manifest and config parse failures are swallowed with except/continue, silently shrinking coverage.
The H10 hook and export reference QueueHudPerformCastSpell, which has no definition.
Contract tests compare locally defined constants or addresses against literals, so they pin nothing in the real code.
Parity tests include TestHarness.h from stub/_shared, which is not present in the snapshot.
